discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, bilayer graphene develops nearly flat electronic bands, in which interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this system and discovered correlated insulating states and, on doping, superconductivity with a phase diagram strikingly reminiscent of the cuprates. This work opened a new field: moire materials in which interaction strength, band topology and carrier density can be tuned in situ in a single device. It has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, nematic and intertwined orders, and fractional Chern insulators without magnetic field. For the first time, the central questions of strongly correlated electron physics, which have resisted resolution for decades, can be studied in a clean, controllable platform. Both the prediction and its experimental realization have had broad, deep and durable impact.
